issues.legal_issue: Daughters who were married before the applicable reform, and whose father was not alive when it commenced, were not entitled to claim a share in ancestral coparcenary property under that reform.
material_facts: The property was ancestral coparcenary property, and the father had died before the reform commenced.
Both daughters had married before the reform commenced.
The daughters sought partition and separate possession of the property.
issues.conclusion: The daughters were not coparceners under the applicable reform and could not claim partition or separate possession of the property on that basis.
issues.legal_principle: Section 29-A(iv) of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956, as inserted by the Hindu Succession (Tamil Nadu Amendment) Act, 1989, excludes a daughter married before the amendment commenced. The Court also applied Prakash v. Phulavati, (2016) 2 SCC 36, as requiring the daughter and coparcener to be living when the relevant amendment commenced. It read Danamma @ Suman Surpur v. Amar, 2018 (1) Scale 657, as not deciding the issue of a coparcener's death before the amendment; Prakash therefore governed that issue.

rule.if: partition_claim_appeal and ancestral_coparcenary_property and (daughters_married_before_reform or father_not_alive_at_reform)

predicates.partition_claim_appeal: The proceeding was an appeal arising from dismissal of a suit seeking partition and separate possession.
predicates.ancestral_coparcenary_property: The property at issue was ancestral property held as coparcenary property.
predicates.daughters_married_before_reform: The daughters seeking a share had married before the reform commenced.
predicates.father_not_alive_at_reform: The father, who was a coparcener, had died before the reform commenced.

issues.definition: When a partition-claim appeal concerns ancestral coparcenary property and either the daughters had married before the reform or their father was no longer alive when it commenced, the daughters have no coparcenary partition entitlement.

issues.legal_issue: A deceased coparcener's share, after division from the coparcenary, devolves as separate property under intestate succession, and a widow's inherited share devolves to her heirs when she later dies.
material_facts: The ancestral coparcenary property had been divided between the father and his son, with each receiving one half.
The father's half became his separate property and, on his death, passed to his widow, two daughters and son under the rules of intestate succession.
On the widow's later death, her inherited share passed to her three children under the rules governing succession to a female Hindu's property.
issues.conclusion: Each daughter received one eighth of the father's half share and one twenty-fourth from the mother's share, for a total of one sixth each. The son received his original one-half share, one eighth from the father's estate and one twenty-fourth from the mother's estate, for a total of two thirds.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 8, 9 and 10 of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956, the father's separate property devolved among his widow and children. Under Sections 15 and 16, the widow's share devolved among her children when she died. The Court treated the father's share obtained on division as separate property, not as continuing coparcenary property.

rule.if: partition_claim_appeal and coparcenary_share_separated_before_death and deceased_left_widow_and_children and widow_later_died

predicates.partition_claim_appeal: The proceeding was an appeal arising from a suit concerning partition and separate possession.
predicates.coparcenary_share_separated_before_death: The coparcenary property had been divided so that the deceased coparcener held a separate share.
predicates.deceased_left_widow_and_children: The deceased left a widow and children entitled to inherit.
predicates.widow_later_died: The widow who inherited a share later died, leaving children who could inherit from her.

issues.definition: When a divided coparcenary share is held separately by a deceased person who leaves a widow and children, and the widow later dies, that separate share and the widow's inherited share devolve to their respective heirs by intestate succession.

issues.legal_issue: A transfer to purchasers may be left undisturbed while persons entitled to a succession share in the transferred property receive the equivalent value of that share.
material_facts: The son had sold portions of the property to purchasers through sale deeds.
The daughters were entitled, through succession, to shares in the relevant property.
The Court decided not to disturb the sales and directed that the daughters receive the value of their legitimate shares in money or equivalent property, with interest.
issues.conclusion: The sales were not to be disturbed; the daughters were entitled to receive the value of their legitimate shares in the sold property, in money or equivalent property, with interest calculated from the sale dates until payment or transfer.
issues.legal_principle: The Court preserved the completed sales and provided an alternative remedy for the daughters' legitimate succession shares, defining those shares by reference to the succession distribution it had set out. It directed valuation by the price prevailing when each sale was made and interest until payment or transfer.

predicates.partition_claim_appeal: The proceeding was an appeal arising from a suit seeking partition and separate possession.
predicates.property_sold_to_purchasers: The property in which a share was claimed had been sold to purchasers.
predicates.claimants_entitled_to_succession_shares_: The claimants had succession rights to shares in the property that had been sold.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns sold property and the claimants have succession shares in it, the sales remain undisturbed and the claimants receive the equivalent value of their shares.
